title: 1992 AMC 8 Problem 22
statement: Eight \(1 \times 1\) square tiles are arranged as shown so their outside edges form a polygon with a perimeter of \(14\) units. Two additional tiles of the same size are added to the figure so that at least one side of each added tile is shared with a side of one of the squares in the original figure. Which of the following could be the perimeter of the new figure?

solutions.text:
A tile that shares exactly one side adds \(2\) to the perimeter (four new edges minus two hidden), while a tile sharing two sides adds \(0.\)

With two added tiles the perimeter can change by \(0,\) \(2,\) or \(4,\) giving new perimeters of \(14,\) \(16,\) or \(18.\) Of the choices, only \(18\) is possible.

Thus, the correct answer is C .
hints: Adding a tile that shares exactly one side changes the perimeter by \(+2\); sharing two sides changes it by \(0\)
With two added tiles, the total change can be \(0,\) \(2,\) or \(4\); add these to \(14\)
